sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who uses the platform, what must it make cheap, and which numbers shape the design?
criteria: Names both users: team leads building coworkers and employees using them
Converts 30,000 tasks a day into peak tasks and model calls per second
Treats a coworker as configuration on a shared runtime rather than a bespoke build
Sets a measurable target for time to build a coworker

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the layers from a Slack, email or ticket message to an action in a system of record.
criteria: Normalizes all three channels into one task with one id
Uses a durable workflow engine for tasks that wait days
Has a skills registry and a scoped memory service as separate layers
Puts policy and identity on the action path

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: Where does firm knowledge come from, and what is read live instead?
criteria: Keeps document ACLs on every indexed chunk
Reads systems of record live rather than indexing them
Takes policies from owned documents, not from conversations

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: How are documents, messages and new memories processed?
criteria: Routes to a coworker by explicit binding before a model classifier
Treats model-extracted memories as proposals validated by rules
Gives a chunk size and embedding store

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: How does a coworker run, which models does it use, and what does it cost?
criteria: Lists cost levers in order with a monthly dollar saving for each
Chooses the model tier by step type in code, not per team
Caps tool calls per task and hands off to a human queue past it
Hands off between coworkers through the workflow with a summary

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What are the memory scopes, and who may write each one?
criteria: Defines at least firm, team, user and coworker scopes
Gives each scope a write rule, with coworkers unable to write firm facts directly
Stores provenance (source, author, expiry) on each fact
Filters scope and tenant in the query, not the prompt

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: What is a skill, and how is it published, pinned and owned?
criteria: Defines a skill manifest with version, tools, scopes, tests and owner
Requires a passing eval suite and review before publishing
Pins skill versions in each coworker and meters usage per version

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: How does each channel connect, and how fast is a simple answer?
criteria: Acknowledges Slack within 3 seconds and replies asynchronously
Lets an approval in one channel resume a task started in another
Gives a stage latency budget under 20 seconds at p95
Applies per-team budgets and concurrency at admission

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: What is cached, and what keeps caches from leaking across permissions?
criteria: Prompt-caches the stable charter and skill prefix
Keys any content cache on the user's ACL or permission set
Caches on-behalf-of tokens with refresh before expiry

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: Where do facts, vectors and tasks live, and what does it all cost?
criteria: Sizes the vector store from chunk count and dimensions
Keeps a fact and its embedding consistent in one transaction or explains how
Keeps EU employees' personal memory in the EU
Gives a monthly total that fits $80k, with non-model prices labeled as assumed

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What does a user or approver receive?
criteria: Replies cite a document or fact id
Action receipts come from the system of record, not model text
Approval requests show the action, amount, recipient and reason

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: Whose identity does a coworker use, and what needs a human?
criteria: Acts on behalf of the requester and never exceeds the requester's permissions
Puts approval thresholds ($1,000, two approvers above a higher amount, external email, HR) in code
Expires approvals and escalates rather than auto-approving
Prevents untrusted inbound email from writing memory or triggering writes

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: How do you prove coworkers save time?
criteria: Measures hours saved from completed tasks times time-study minutes
Excludes tasks that a human had to redo
Tracks build time and cost per completed task

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks, and what does the platform do?
criteria: Covers memory poisoning with a way to revoke facts by source
Covers a skill regression with a canary and rollback
Never auto-approves on timeout

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: In what order do you build it in six months?
criteria: Builds the durable task workflow and identity first
Migrates the existing coworkers before launching new ones
Ends each phase with a measured number
